title: Two-stage OTA, cascode compensation
description: The Ahuja (cascode) variant of the two-stage Miller OTA: the compensation cap $C_c$ returns to a low-impedance cascode node instead of directly across the second stage. Routing the compensation current through the common-gate cascode blocks the feedforward path, so the right-half-plane zero that plagues plain Miller compensation is removed and the pole-splitting is better damped — for the same GBW the phase margin comes almost entirely from the second pole. The stage structure mirrors the plain Miller OTA (stage-1 input pair + mirror load, stage-2 common source + load); the added cascode device carries the stage-1 branch current and provides the node $C_c$ returns through. The stage-1 mirror load is diode-bound: at DC balance its output side sits at exactly the diode drop (the zero-systematic-offset condition), so the stage-1 output DC is $VDD - |V_{GS,ld1}|$ by construction rather than a number to retune. Entered from the COMMON MODE like the 5T: the input pair's tail node is pinned so the produced $CM_{in}$ equals $CM_{dc}$. The pole and phase-margin rows are ESTIMATE-grade small-signal approximations; the simulator owns stability sign-off. On the demo NMOS table the polarity-inverted devices keep their sign params at +1.

params.name: PM_target
params.note: phase-margin target; cascode comp removes the RHP zero so a higher target is realistic. Estimate-grade

params.name: C1_est
params.note: stage-1 output node cap (stage-2 gate + parasitics + wiring); refine from the stage-2 cgg plus extraction

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis This sheet carries NO containment edges: stage 1 does not close on sky130-class supplies at these defaults, and a range claim that cannot be tuned honestly would be theater — see the single-stage OTAs for the pattern.

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the input pair's tail node. Solved rather than set: bisected between min and max (the BRACKET) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. Fixes the pair's body bias and drain-source voltage in one stroke. Both bracket ends must leave the pair drain-source voltage under the mirror diode drop — on a process whose PMOS diode eats most of the rail, the pin will say so. This variant stacks the cascode node in the same budget, so raising gm_id_ld1 for a smaller diode drop is the right direction but does not get there alone: on a sky130 tt realization it closes only past the knob's own maximum. Lowering V_casc toward its floor is the second knob, and the two together are what reopen the budget

params.name: Cc
params.note: cascode compensation cap: sets the dominant pole and GBW = gm1/(2*pi*Cc)

params.name: V_casc
params.note: cascode node vds (the low-impedance node Cc returns through)

params.name: out_sign
params.note: vds sign of the stage-2 device table: +1 N-style, -1 signed-PMOS

doc.title: Stage-1 mirror-load device
doc.description: One side of the stage-1 mirror load at half the tail current; its diode drop sets the stage-1 output DC and its output conductance loads the first stage.

doc.title: Stage-1 input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current. Its source sits at the tail node — that is its body bias — and its drain sits one compensation-cascode drop BELOW the stage-1 output (the cascode is in series in this branch), so its drain-source voltage is what is left after both the mirror diode drop and V_casc.

doc.title: Compensation cascode device
doc.description: The common-gate cascode carrying the stage-1 branch current; the compensation cap returns to its low-impedance source, so the feedforward path (and the RHP zero) is blocked.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

params.name: vsbx
params.note: the source stands on the input device's drain node, not the bulk

doc.title: Stage-2 common-source device
doc.description: The second-stage gain device carrying the full stage-2 current at the output DC level; its gm sets the second pole and its gate cap dominates the stage-1 output node.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

rows.name: CM_in
rows.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting; rises monotonically with the tail node, so the pin is a well-posed bisection

rows.name: V1
rows.note: stage-1 output DC — the mirror diode drop below the supply, by construction rather than retuned: at balance the mirror's output side sits exactly there (also the zero-systematic-offset condition)

rows.name: gm2
rows.note: stage-2 transconductance sets the second pole

rows.name: gm_casc
rows.note: cascode transconductance (sets the impedance of the node Cc returns to)

rows.name: GBW
rows.note: compensated unity-gain bandwidth (input gm into the compensation cap)

rows.name: p2
rows.note: non-dominant pole ESTIMATE; cascode compensation both removes the RHP zero and pushes this pole out — refine C1_est from the stage-2 cgg plus extraction

rows.name: PM
rows.note: ESTIMATE: only the second-pole phase lag remains because the cascode blocks the feedforward RHP zero. Small-signal approximation — the simulator owns stability sign-off

rows.name: SR
rows.note: the smaller slew limit: stage-1 tail charging Cc, or stage-2 current charging CL

rows.name: Av1
rows.note: stage-1 gain into the input-device and mirror-load output conductances

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: the resistance the amplifier presents at its output — stage two's own output conductance in parallel with its load device's. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

rows.name: Av2
rows.note: stage-2 common-source gain into its own and the load conductances

rows.name: Av
rows.note: two-stage DC gain (product of the stage gains)

rows.name: cgg2
rows.note: stage-2 gate capacitance — the dominant term in the stage-1 output cap C1_est

rows.name: cgg_in
rows.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single input device. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

rules.note: two-stage DC gain meets the target
the worse of the two slew limits meets the target
the compensated bandwidth (gm1/(2*pi*Cc)) meets the target
ESTIMATE-grade phase margin (no RHP zero term); the simulator owns the real stability sign-off
stage-2 device saturated at the output DC level
stage-2 load saturated at the output DC level
the cascode device stays saturated at its node vds
trips when the tail node is pushed so high the pair runs out of drain-source voltage under the mirror diode drop — lower gm/ID on the mirror spends less of it

the stage-2 gate sits at V1 = VDD - |vgs_ld1|, so stage 2 carries its intended current only when its own |vgs| at (I2, gm_id_s2) matches the mirror diode drop — the classic W/L-ratio condition. Retune gm_id_s2 or I2 until these agree, or the second stage sits at a different current than the sheet assumes
